_comment: FROZEN reaction / front-run source-reputation-filter constants. DO NOT EDIT (retune) after the
first reaction edge-proof run. This is the audit-parity twin of MOMENTUM_PARAMS.frozen.json,
REALIZABLE_EXIT_PARAMS.frozen.json, and baseline.frozen.json: it externalizes the reaction
harness's model constants so they are a declared, change-controlled artifact rather than magic
numbers buried in code (anti-p-hacking, red-team flaw 2A).
The canonical hash in `frozen_hash` is recomputed deterministically from `params` alone
(aats/backtest/reaction_harness.py: _canonical_reaction_hash); a test FAILS if any hashed value
drifts. The threshold is a Decimal-as-STRING (never float); counts are int; the policy flag is
bool (data-models.md §0).
THE MODEL RULE (reaction_harness.py, decide_reaction_entry): the BASELINE follows EVERY signal.
The MODEL follows every signal EXCEPT it DECLINES a signal whose source has a PROVEN track record
(>= `min_prior_signals` eligible strictly-prior + already-observed same-source outcomes) whose
MEAN realized net-PnL-per-SOL is BELOW `reputation_threshold`. Below the track-record floor the
source is on the NEUTRAL PRIOR (`neutral_prior_selects`). The model is a strict SUBSET of the
baseline (it can only DE-RISK — drop proven-loser sources — never add a signal). The reputation
is MONEY (mean net-PnL-per-SOL), NEVER a win-rate.
ENTRY realism: `entry_latency_haircut_bps` worsens the front-run entry fill (fill HIGHER than the
signal tick — the reaction has already begun moving the price). Conservative: it can only LOWER
realized PnL, never fabricate a GO. Distinct from the ~6% cost stack's AMM entry slippage.
FROZEN — MUST NOT BE TUNED AGAINST THE CORPUS. Changing a value here is p-hacking the selection
against the scoreboard; it is a TEST FAILURE, not an edit. Open an ADR + delta notice instead.
See aats/models/artifacts/MODEL_CARD_reaction.md.

params_provenance.reputation_threshold: The net-PnL-per-SOL floor a source's PROVEN track record must clear for the model to keep following it. '0' = do not follow a source whose realized prior track record is net-negative per SOL — a structural floor, NOT a fitted level. Decimal-as-string, never float. A signed money-per-risk ratio, never a win-rate.
params_provenance.min_prior_signals: How many ELIGIBLE (strictly-prior signal_block_time < current AND already-observed outcome_resolved <= current) same-source outcomes are required before the reputation threshold gate applies. Below this a source is on the NEUTRAL PRIOR. 3 = a minimal track record before demoting a source. Illustrative structural constant, NOT fitted. Integer.
params_provenance.neutral_prior_selects: The neutral-prior policy: whether a source with too short a track record is FOLLOWED. true = innocent-until-proven-loser (the model only demotes a source once it has PROVEN itself a net loser over min_prior_signals outcomes), keeping the model a strict de-risk subset of the follow-every-signal baseline. Bool.
params_provenance.entry_latency_haircut_bps: Front-run entry-latency haircut (bps): a real bot cannot fill at the exact signal tick, so entry_fill = signal_price_sol * (1 + bps/10000) (fill HIGHER = worse). 50 bps (0.5%) models the few-hundred-ms lag while the reaction begins. Conservative — can only LOWER realized PnL, never fabricate a GO. Distinct from and stacks with the ~6% cost stack's AMM entry slippage. Integer bps.

baseline_rule: follow EVERY signal — enter on every recorded signal at a fixed per-trade risk. No free numeric parameter; it is the strict superset of the model's selection.
invariant: MODEL selection is a strict SUBSET of the BASELINE selection (the model can only DECLINE a proven-loser source, never add a signal). GATE-B therefore measures exactly: does demoting proven-loser sources beat following every signal, net of cost, per unit risk?
